mappings.note: Rank the five oceans by size - naming and ordering the ocean set that LO-5 asks pupils to place on the world map. Not LO-2, nothing about life or the spheres.
Ocean-born clouds bringing the monsoon to India: the water cycle sustaining life on land, which is the habitability sense of LO-2. Not LO-7, since no Indian landform is located.
Explains at length why the continent count runs four to seven - how the continents of LO-5 are conventionally divided.
Why Eurasia is split into Europe and Asia; the same convention question narrowed to one case, still continent identification under LO-5.
Names the five inhabited continents behind the Olympic rings - a continent-recall item, so LO-5 rather than any culture outcome.
The significance of India's Antarctic research is India's contribution in science, which LO-24 names. Not LO-5: Antarctica is the setting, but the question is about India's scientific work there.
Oceans absorbing solar radiation and carbon dioxide and driving weather - the ocean's part in keeping the earth habitable, so LO-2. Not LO-5, no ocean is located.

Oceans as highways for migration and trade is about the earth as the habitat of human beings and the distribution of its resources, which only the goal CG-SST1 states; LO-2 is narrower (life and the biosphere) and would misdescribe a question about human movement and commerce.
Why World Oceans Day is kept - the ocean as a source of food, medicine and oxygen and its part in the biosphere, which is LO-2's own word.
How plastic waste injures marine animals and enters the food chain: direct harm to the biosphere. Not CG-SST1, because the question stays on living things rather than on human use of the sea.
Overfishing as depletion faster than stocks can breed, disrupting marine ecosystems - again the biosphere of LO-2. Not C-SST4.1, whose subject is why given occupations exist in rural and urban areas.
Names both Indian island groups AND the water bodies they sit in, so LO-7 for the Indian features and LO-5 for the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea.

Compares the land and water share of the two hemispheres - world-map distribution (LO-5) framed by the Equator (LO-6). Kept apart from the item that asks about the climatic EFFECT of that imbalance, which draws in LO-2 instead.
Groundwater as fresh water held in soil and rock - a component of the earth's water zones. Not LO-5, which concerns surface oceans on the world map.
Analyses ocean boundaries as map conventions rather than natural divides; the subject is how the oceans of LO-5 are delimited, even though the supporting argument mentions currents and marine life.

Three ways the sea shaped human societies - exploration, trade and food, plus myth and art. That spans the goal's 'habitat of humans and the spatial distribution of its resources' and is served by no single outcome, so the goal is cited, as with the migration-and-trade item.

The Indian Ocean's role for India, worked through the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal (LO-5) and India's coasts, ports and island territories (LO-7). Not LO-24: the monsoon and trade are geography, not a scientific contribution.

Why protecting the marine environment needs cross-border cooperation - pollution and overfishing are transboundary harms to the biosphere, which is LO-2. The tsunami half of the question has no outcome in this frame; the marine-protection half carries the mapping.
Reasons from continent SIZE, read off the chapter diagram (LO-5), to climate range and biodiversity (LO-2). Neither outcome alone covers the inference the item asks for.
The value of the Indian Antarctic Programme and its ice-core climate research: India's contribution in science under LO-24, the same reading as the shorter Dakshin Gangotri items.

Takes the uneven hemispheric split of land and water (LO-5) and asks what it does to climate and currents, i.e. to the conditions for life (LO-2). The plain description of that split was mapped to LO-5 with LO-6 instead, since it stops at the distribution.
The water cycle carrying ocean water to the continents as fresh water - the movement between the earth's water zones that makes land life possible, so LO-2.
Human-induced threats to the ocean and their long-term cost to biodiversity and ocean health; a biosphere argument, broader than the single plastic and overfishing items but under the same outcome.
Compares Greenland, a world-map island (LO-5), with Lakshadweep, an Indian island group (LO-7). The single-island items got one code each; this one genuinely needs both.
Uses the Europe/Asia split to argue that continent boundaries are interpretations - still about how the continents of LO-5 are defined, at greater length than the short version.
Case study reading land and water shares off a world map by hemisphere: distribution of continents and oceans (LO-5) against the Equator (LO-6). Mapped like the hemisphere-comparison short answer.
A coastal community losing catch to overfishing and plastic - marine fauna and threats to it (LO-2) - with one sub-part asking which arm of the Indian Ocean the east coast faces (LO-5).

Whether a sea is part of an ocean, which ocean is largest, and whether the oceans are one connected body: all questions about the ocean set of LO-5. Not LO-2, since the marine-life mention is only supporting detail.
